title: Fleet drain-rate SLA proxy and staged prewarm scheduler
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Planned maintenance and unplanned host drains cause transient throughput drops that violate per-customer throughput guarantees and increase tail latency. Existing drain logic focuses on simple host evacuation and reactive prewarm; it does not coordinate with throughput contracts or perform predictive KV cache warming. This ticket proposes a two-part system: (1) a lightweight SLA proxy that enforces throughput reservations and gracefully shapes traffic during drains, and (2) a staged prewarm scheduler that predicts and warms KV caches for affected sessions/tenants before traffic shifts.

Goals: 
- Prevent customer-level throughput SLO breaches during node drains/upgrades by ensuring reserved throughput lanes are honored or replaced.
- Reduce post-drain latency spikes by increasing KV cache warmup success for rerouted requests.
- Integrate with autoscaler signals and maintenance windows so drains can be scheduled with minimal customer impact.

Design overview: 
1) SLA proxy (control-plane component):
   - Maintains per-customer (or per-route) throughput contracts derived from Dedicated reservations.
   - When a host/node is marked for drain, evaluates active allocations and computes a shortfall vector (tokens/sec or qps).
   - If shortfall > threshold, enacts one of: reserve capacity elsewhere, throttle non-guaranteed traffic, or preempt lower-tier work.
   - Exposes enforcement mode flags: dry-run (observe), advisory (dashboard alerts), enforce (apply shaping).

2) Staged prewarm scheduler (orchestration agent):
   - Consumes drain plan and historical traffic profiles to rank sessions/routes by cache sensitivity.
   - Schedules prewarm jobs in waves: small fast warm for hottest prefixes, broader KV preheat for top-N sessions, and background fill for long-tail.
   - Uses backoff-aware pacing to avoid overload during concurrent drains across the fleet.

Telemetry and acceptance metrics: 
- No >5% increase in p95 latency for reserved customers during a standard 30-minute maintenance wave compared to baseline.
- KV cache hit-rate on rerouted traffic increases by >=20% within first 2 minutes after drain when prewarm is enabled.
- SLO violation rate for throughput guarantees reduced by >=90% in canary.

Implementation plan: 
- Week 1: Prototype SLA proxy simulation and offline drain shortfall calculator (ENG-198765-branch).
- Week 2: Implement initial enforcement hooks and advisory mode; add dashboard panels.
- Week 3: Build staged prewarm scheduler MVP, integrate with KV-cache priming API, add pacing policies.
- Week 4: Canary with 10% of Dedicated fleets (low-impact tenants) in advisory -> enforce progression.

Rollout & safety: 
- Start in dry-run with metrics-only mode for 2 weeks.
- Gradual ramp: advisory -> soft-enforce (throttle non-reserved) -> enforce (reserve & preempt) with ops approval.
- Auto-rollback if p95 latency or error rates increase >15% over baseline for >10 minutes.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Over-enthusiastic prewarming can starve capacity: use autoscaler feedback and prewarm rate-limits.
- Incorrect shortfall calc could preempt too much traffic: keep advisory mode and human-in-loop for first canaries.
- Edge cases with multi-tenant hosts: ensure tenant isolation checks and per-tenant quotas.

Open questions: 
- Mapping from 'throughput reservation' to concrete tokens/sec: use existing accounting or create short-lived reservation tokens?
- How to prioritize mixed SLA nodes with many small reservations?

Acceptance criteria (PR/Feature): 
- Code merged for SLA proxy and scheduler in runtime-orchestration repo.
- End-to-end canary metrics meet acceptance thresholds above.
- Runbook updated with playbook for disabling/enabling enforcement.
